pr_title: importccl: remove support for non-bundle IMPORT TABLE
pr_body:
A non-bundle import refers to the flavour of IMPORT that
has separate sources for table creation and data ingestion.

A bundle import on the other hand refers to the flavour of
IMPORT that reads both the schema and data from the same source.

Prior to this change a user could specify the schema of the table
being imported into in two ways:
- inline definition of the table schema in the IMPORT TABLE command.
- IMPORT TABLE ... CREATE USING syntax to point to a file containing a
`CREATE TABLE` statement that defines the table schema.

Import would then use this schema to first create a table and then import
the data from the data source. Table creation in IMPORT was backed by custom
table creation logic that attempted to mirror SQL support for `CREATE TABLE`
statements. Historically, this always fell behind fixes and additional features
that were added to `CREATE TABLE`, resulting in a poor UX when
atttempting to create and import into a table, using a single IMPORT command.

This change removes support for:
- `IMPORT TABLE ... CREATE USING`
- `IMPORT TABLE ... <non-bundle-format> DATA`

`non-bundle-format` refers to CSV, Delimited, PGCOPY, AVRO. These
formats do not define the table schema in the same file as the data.

The workaround following this feature removal is to use `CREATE TABLE` with
the same schema that was previously being passed into the IMPORT statement,
followed by an `IMPORT INTO` the newly created table.

Fixes: #70050

- `IMPORT TABLE ... CREATE USING`
- `IMPORT TABLE ... <non-bundle-format> DATA`

`non-bundle-format` refers to CSV, Delimited, PGCOPY, AVRO. These
formats do not define the table schema in the same file as the data.

The workaround following this feature removal is to use `CREATE TABLE` with
the same schema that was previously being passed into the IMPORT statement,
followed by an `IMPORT INTO` the newly created table.

issue_context.title: importccl: delete IMPORT TABLE code
issue_context.body:
In 21.2 we deprecated `IMPORT TABLE` and encouraged users to use `CREATE TABLE` + `IMPORT INTO`. This is because we have historically found `IMPORT TABLE` falling behind new features added to `CREATE TABLE`. This has led to UX surprises and nil pointer exceptions across past releases of CockroachDB. Import should be in the business of ingesting large amounts of data. Creating a table with a given schema should be the responsibility of `CREATE TABLE`. Going forward we believe that investing time in making `IMPORT INTO` more featureful is more productive, and will lead to a better user experience.

This issue tracks the deletion of all `IMPORT TABLE` code in 22.1. We should also take the opportunity to refactor parts of import, the `importPlanHook` in particular, as they have become rather unwieldy.

Epic CRDB-10307
